title: Fire twucks! Fire twucks! (sic)
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss fire trucks versus fire engines, starting with the distinction: a fire engine is a vehicle built around a water tank, pump and hoses, while a fire truck carries ladders, rescue and forcible-entry equipment. They trace history from water pumps dragged on sleds and pulled by people and horses, through steam and early motorized vehicles around 1911, to ladder technology driven by skyscrapers and the modern fire engine of the 1960s. They cover fire engine components (water tank, pump, hoses, deluge gun, drop tank), how crews operate the pump, foam types, cherry picker aerial buckets, outriggers, hydraulic ladders, tiller trucks, and the tools fire trucks carry. The episode ends with a listener mail from Hannah McAdams in Dublin about a French film, The Officer's Award, and a war mask.
topics: difference between fire truck and fire engine

segments.title: Opening banter and fire truck enthusiasm
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with light banter about loving fire trucks, a family anecdote involving a daughter and FaceTime, and dogs reacting to sirens. They set up the episode's question of fire truck versus fire engine.

segments.title: Fire truck vs. fire engine distinction
segments.summary: The hosts explain that a fire engine is built around a water tank and pump to deliver water to a fire, while a fire truck carries ladders, firefighters and rescue equipment. A fire truck may arrive after the engine.
topics: difference between fire truck and fire engine

segments.title: History of fire engines
segments.summary: Early fire engines were water pumps on sleds dragged by people, later pulled by horses, which tired on long runs. Steam trucks were unreliable. Motorized combustion vehicles arrived around 1911, and skyscrapers later drove ladder technology. Horse-drawn and steam equipment gave way to motor-powered trucks in the 1910s through the 1930s.

segments.title: Fire apparatus types, bucket brigades, and cherry pickers
segments.summary: Fire trucks are specialized for water, equipment, or ladders, and local fleets depend on funding and population. The hosts discuss a city-building game about fires, the bucket brigade, and post-World War Two cherry picker aerial buckets used for rescues, along with the 1960s origins of the modern fire engine.

segments.title: Fire engine components and water supply
segments.summary: A fire engine has three core components: a water tank, a pump that pressurizes water, and hoses or lines. The pump uses centrifugal force from an impeller. Crews use onboard water first, then connect to hydrants, ponds or pools, and may set up a drop tank as a temporary holding pool.

segments.title: Hoses, nozzles and the deluge gun
segments.summary: Engines carry many hoses of varying lengths and diameters, color-coded and often pre-connected, plus booster lines, curb jumpers, hose packs and ladder-mounted lines. The deluge gun on top of the engine sends large volumes of water far. Nozzles include piercing nozzles that shoot through walls.

segments.title: Foam, outriggers, ladders and fire truck tools
segments.summary: Foam is used for Class A and Class B fires, with some concerns about toxicity to water supplies and protein-based options. Ladders extend up to about 150 feet hydraulically and are stabilized by outriggers with pads. Fire trucks carry tools such as the Halligan tool, pike poles, bolt cutters, sledgehammers, chainsaws, and jaws of life, and carry EMS equipment.
topics: Class A and Class B foam

segments.title: Smoke damage, tiller trucks and wrap-up
segments.summary: The hosts discuss smoke damage to property, with a personal anecdote about a smoke-filled condo. They cover tiller trucks, where the rear-wheel driver steers opposite to the front, and why tillers help navigate city streets. They close the discussion of firefighting with humor about touring fire stations.

segments.title: Listener mail: The Officer's Award and war masks
segments.summary: Listener Hannah McAdams in Dublin writes about a book on so-called whistlers, German soldiers with throat injuries, and recommends the French film The Officer's Award, about a French engineer injured in World War One and treated with a war mask.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts direct listeners to the website and email for contact and close the episode.
